note: Source: Dopmeijer JM et al. (2022) PLOS ONE 17(12):e0267175 (CC BY 4.0), S1 File (.s001, SPSS .sav); data/dopmeijer_2022_burnout_battery.py. mapping_basis=data_labels: the IRW item codes ARE the .sav column names (the script melts Loneliness_A..K unrenamed, no positional or renaming step), and each column carries a variable label giving its item text, so code-to-text is tied at the source. item_text is those labels transcribed VERBATIM, including the file's own typos -- 'There are enough people woth whom I feel close' (H), 'I often feel abondoned' (J), 'cosyness' (E); nothing was normalised or upgraded to canonical wording. LANGUAGE FALLBACK: the study was administered online to Dutch students at Windesheim/HAN universities of applied sciences, so the administered wording is Dutch, but neither the deposit nor the paper's supplements carries it -- S1 File is the only supplement and all 11 variable labels are English (the authors' own rendering). Per SKILL.md core model 4 this is the fallback: English in the base fields, language=Dutch, _translated columns empty, text_source=translated_substitute. For a later backfill, the canonical Dutch wording IS published, off-source, in Van Tilburg & de Jong Gierveld's own Manual of the Loneliness Scale (home.fsw.vu.nl/tg.van.tilburg/manual_loneliness_scale_1999.html; archived copy at web.archive.org/web/20240520183843) which prints all 11 items in Dutch and English -- e.g. item 3 'Ik ervaar een leegte om me heen' / 'I experience a general sense of emptiness'. The study's English labels are recognisably independent translations of that same Dutch (D: 'in geval van narigheid' -> 'in case of bad circumstances'), and the A..K order matches the canonical 1..11 order exactly: the .sav's own LON_B/C/E/F/I/J_mirrored columns, labelled 'positively formulated', are precisely the six canonically negative items 2,3,5,6,9,10. RESP DIRECTION IS REVERSED relative to the source and the paper, deliberately, by the processing script: the .sav's value labels read 1='Yes! Totally agree!' ... 5='No! Totally disagree!' and the paper says 'All items were scored from 1 (Yes! Totally agree) to 5 (No! Totally disagree)', but MAP_LON in the .py re-maps the label strings so IRW stores 1='No! Totally disagree!' ... 5='Yes! Totally agree!'. The shipped option_text follows the LIVE data, checked cell for cell (route 9, all 55 item x level counts identical; the reversed reading is off by 41,586). RIGHTS checked before transcribing: no clause fires. The wording IRW copied comes from a CC BY 4.0 PLOS deposit. The rights holder's own manual states only 'The scale is available for scientific research programs, under the following conditions: a. The source of the scale should be mentioned ...', that it may be used in survey research, and that it is 'not permissible' to use it to diagnose loneliness in individuals without consultation -- no non-commercial clause, no redistribution bar, no fee, and no copyright/permission statement anywhere in the manual (grepped). wording_rights is therefore not set; flagged in notes so a human can override if 'available for scientific research programs' is read as an NC statement. instructions/section_prompt left blank: the deposit publishes none, and the manual's administration instructions were not imported since they are off-source like the Dutch item wording. correct_response blank (no correct answer). One irw_fetch export (34,551 rows) was spent deliberately, to get the per-item x per-level counts route 9 needs; the gate itself ran with --table-sets.
